prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (alias Ironwood): auto start by demand/channel depth; permissives suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips; lost permissive -> alarm/stop; maintenance release only after isolations tagged, locally verified, acknowledged in shift turnover record. Raw Water Screen Channel: sends Rake Torque Snapshot to Maintenance Planner; high-high level needs field confirmation. Coagulant Dosing Skid (alias Marigold): sends Alum Batch Ticket on new lot to Laboratory Technician; dose trim by analyzer/operator targets. North Filter Gallery (alias Cobalt): per-filter turbidity/headloss. South Filter Gallery: sends Filter Run Exception Note. Washed filter returns only when rinse-to-waste meets target. Chlorine Contact Basin: produces Chlorine Residual Alarm; maintains contact time for production rate/level/residual; chlorine feed adjusted gradually. Clearwell Level Controller: keeps storage within limits; low-level interlock stops pumps below safe minimum; high-level alarm for production reduction before overflow. Backwash Recovery Tank. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (alias Sparrow): sends Jar Test Photograph Set; available for maintenance return samples. SCADA Historian Server (alias Lantern): retains audit data and pre/post-work performance. Actors: Chief Operator (modes, targets; decides isolation/restricted operation on failed post-maintenance test; confirms disinfection controls consistent in Historian before normal service); Duty Engineer; Maintenance Planner (alias Quarry); Laboratory Technician (sends Sample Chain Slip; confirms sampling needs, acceptance concerns, confirmatory residuals on drift/fouling); Distribution Dispatcher; Chemical Supplier Driver (sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log); Residuals Hauler; auditors; craft worker. Modes: automatic; Manual override; Reduced-capacity; Storm Intake Mode (more sampling, discretionary work re-reviewed). Reqs: analyzer loss -> safe dose plus grabs; Chlorine Residual Alarm pauses maintenance task, verify sample flow vs grab, hold production increase; return to service only after jumpers/bypasses/tools/barriers removed or accepted, with evidence (inspection, tests, samples, operator acceptance); failed test keeps work order open.

Document units:
S134: The Clearwell Level Controller sends the Clearwell Diver Entry Permit when level and isolation prerequisites have been verified by the control system.
S135: Clearwell level changes are trended against filter production and high-service demand so that slow instrumentation errors can be distinguished from actual storage changes.
S136: The High Service Pump Header is identified in voice radio traffic by the alias Juniper when operators need a short confirmation name.
S137: The High Service Pump Header sequences available pumps to meet distribution demand while avoiding unnecessary starts, short cycling, and operation near unstable portions of the pump curves.
S138: Lead and lag pump assignments are rotated according to runtime, availability, and any operating restriction entered by the Chief Operator.
S139: Header pressure control uses a paced response so that pump starts, pump speed changes, and valve movements do not create avoidable pressure transients in the distribution system.
S140: The High Service Pump Header produces the Pump Bearing Vibration Clip after a configured vibration threshold is exceeded during pump operation.
S141: If a high-service pump trips, the remaining available pumps are evaluated automatically against the current pressure setpoint before another unit is started.
S142: The North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station receive pressure support through coordinated setpoints that reflect system demand and storage conditions.
S143: The Distribution Dispatcher is identified by the alias Falcon during pressure coordination calls with plant staff.
S144: The Distribution Dispatcher communicates expected demand changes, main break impacts, and pressure complaints so that plant pumping decisions match field conditions.
S145: During Storm Intake Mode, operators watch the relationship between raw water quality, filter loading, disinfectant demand, and high-service pumping to avoid forcing production beyond treatment capability.
S146: Abnormal clearwell level, loss of residual, loss of pump header pressure, or conflicting instrument readings require the Duty Engineer to review the operating condition before setpoints are changed outside normal ranges.
S147: The SCADA Historian Server stores residual, level, pressure, and pump status data at sufficient resolution to support event reconstruction after alarms or customer pressure complaints.
S148: Manual operation is allowed only when the operator can maintain residual targets, clearwell limits, and distribution pressure with direct observation of the affected indications.
S149: Return to automatic control requires stable chlorine residual, stable clearwell level response, and confirmed high-service pressure control for a period set by the Chief Operator.
